name: Admin Document List
description: View admin documents in the fixed business column order Actions, Title, States, Created, Client and Project. The table requests server-owned pages of 10 rows and the grid requests 12; the authoritative range and total appear in pagination, ?page restores the same cut, and changing folder, project, filters, search, order or presentation requests the matching server page. Rapid navigation cancels the superseded request so an older folder cannot repaint the latest selection. Created is the only sortable column: it opens newest-first, toggles both date directions from an accessible icon, serializes only the non-default ?order=oldest value and keeps that value across filters, folders, scope, search and presentation changes. Archived rows sort by archived_at, active rows by created_at and mixed/search results use the date each row displays. Gallery and compact layouts expose the same date direction through a toolbar control because they have no column header. Ordinary documents show workflow episodes; collection accounts instead show their derived commercial state (Borrador, Emitida, Enviada, Envío fallido, Pagada or Anulada), and issued accounts expose only read-only viewing, one accounting PDF download and archive/restore actions. The exclusive cycle appears before additive signals, every badge carries its open duration, Solucionar bug is visually prominent, overflow collapses to +N, and documents with no cycle show Por clasificar. The kebab action keeps the contextual accessible name Acciones de <title>, omits the native title and exposes exactly one short application tooltip, Acciones, before opening the row menu. Landscape keeps Title, States, Created and Actions as columns while grouping Client/Project under Title; compact cards keep Title/States primary and order secondary metadata as Created, Client, Project. Filters and episode behavior are covered by admin-document-state-filters and admin-document-state-workflow. Los encabezados de carpeta contienen nombres largos de proyecto sin ampliar la página; conservan navegación y acceso a documentos.
